summary: Mark Twain National Forest's 100-foot steel tower, built around 1934 or 1939 (the sources differ); staffed intermittently until 2019; restoration planned pending approvals.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower with lookout stand and fire finder
facts.agency: USDA Forest Service, Mark Twain National Forest (Eleven Point Ranger District)

events.note: Forest Lookouts gives 1934 for the 100-foot steel tower but names no source
Picnic grounds at the site developed by the Forest Service; a recreation area at the tower was opened in October 1938
Register says likely constructed by the Bartlett CCC Camp 3752 in 1939, with a towerman's residence, garage and recreation site
Towerman 'Smoky Joe' Steininger pictured at work in a Chicago Daily News picture reprinted by The Current Local
Lookout used for prescribed fire monitoring from 2016
Staffed intermittently until 2019; a longtime employee's retirement left it vacant

notes_for_editor: Two disputes left open. Build year: the register says 'likely' 1939 (Bartlett CCC camp); Forest Lookouts gives 1934 with no source; both are shown. County: the register says Shannon County, Forest Lookouts says Carter County (27N-2W-31); the story avoids naming a county. No current visiting or rental information was found; the register says restoration is planned. Two Facebook items (Shannon County Museum, Ozarks History Archives) appeared only in search snippets and were not used. Confidence is medium because of the unresolved county and build year. Fact-check 2026-10-09: two story sentences that closely copied register wording were reworded, and the summary now says restoration is planned pending approvals and that staffing was intermittent.
